source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: 1108's XPCOM SaveMessage bridge reads the input synchronously, owns callbacks with RefPtr, and detaches a moz_task so the async operation outlives the call. Returning Ok only means that scheduling succeeded. The historical outer save_message reports OnStartCopy, maps the inner Result to a status, and calls OnStopCopy; it aborts early if OnStartCopy itself fails. Current CreateMessage keeps a detached task but uses a safe create listener and a different completion framework. Preserve the asynchronous completion contract without copying the retired callback architecture.
title: Distinguish scheduled EWS work from successful remote completion
